issues.text: Contact validation with Organisation Acme, email person@company.com, and phone 123456 remained on Contact but showed only “Enter a valid phone number”; no visible email validation error appeared, cont

On Payment with Alice Standard and Bob Workshop (Attendees 2, Subtotal $380.00), applying promo code TEAM15 displayed “That promo code is not recognised.” and left Discount −$0.00 and Total due $380.0
Payment displays a zero discount as “−$0.00”; intended zero-discount state is $0.00 without a negative sign.

Submitting Contact with Acme, person@company.com, and 123456 remains on Contact and shows both the required email and phone validation errors. — After the submission, step 5 records that Contact still shows the entered values but “only the phone validation message” is visible, so the required email error was missing.
Applying the specified valid promo code TEAM15 immediately displays “That promo code is not recognised.” and leaves discount at −$0.00 and total due at $240.00 for two Standard attendees.
Visible form labels are not programmatically associated: Organisation and Phone inputs are exposed as unnamed textboxes.

Applying a valid TEAM15 promo allows registration to be confirmed and produces a confirmation panel whose attendee count, organisation, seats, and total match Payment. — At steps 9-10, Payment showed TEAM15 rejected with $0.00 discount and $240.00 total, and clicking Confirm registration produced no DOM change or confirmation panel.

For one Standard ($120) and one Workshop ($260) attendee, TEAM15 applies a $57.00 discount and produces a $323.00 total from the $380.00 subtotal. — Steps 35-37 established the correctly reconciled $380.00 subtotal for Standard plus Workshop, but Apply showed “That promo code is not recognised.” and retained a $0.00 discount rather than the required $57.00/$323.00 result.
Validation error remains after its field is corrected: valid “Alex Rivera” still shows “Full name is required.”
After email is corrected to alex@example.com, the stale “Enter a valid email address.” error remains visible.
Duplicate-submit protection failed: two rapid Place order clicks created BK-1001 and BK-1002 receipts.

Rapidly clicking Place order twice with valid default billing details produces exactly one confirmation and exactly one receipt. — After the two clicks in steps 7-8, step 9 observes two receipt rows: "BK-1001 — $1002.90 to finance@northwind.test" and "BK-1002 — $1002.90 to finance@northwind.test".
Row and select-all checkboxes are exposed as unnamed controls, so selection actions lack accessible labels.

Closing the selected Export never finishes and Cannot reset password tickets reports “Closed 1 ticket(s)” while retaining their Closed statuses and clearing selection. — After the close action, step 9 observed both tickets still Closed with selections cleared and the feedback “Closed 0 ticket(s),” rather than the expected 1.

Priority filtering produces the specified matching ticket sets without extra rows or missing expected rows. — With High selected, step 13 observed 3 High rows rather than the expected 2, and with Normal plus Open only, step 17 observed only Billing address rejected rather than the expected SSO login loop and Billing address rejected.
Select-all checkbox remains checked after changing the subject filter from Invoice to SSO, even though the newly visible SSO ticket is unchecked and only the two hidden prior tickets are selected.

When changing the subject filter from Invoice to SSO, select-all and the newly shown SSO ticket are unchecked until the user selects it. — Step 21 observes SSO login loop with its row checkbox unchecked but the select-all checkbox checked before the SSO row is clicked.
Clicking Export CSV shows visible feedback reading “Export queued.” — Step 2 clicked Export CSV and immediately inspected feedback, but recorded domChanged=NO and no visible feedback observation.
Clicking Send to stakeholders shows visible feedback reading “Report sent.” — Step 3 clicked Send to stakeholders, but recorded domChanged=NO and no visible feedback observation.
Export CSV shows a queued confirmation message when clicked. — Step 2 directly clicked Export CSV and immediately inspected feedback, but recorded domChanged=NO and no queued message observation.

Send to stakeholders shows a sent confirmation message when clicked. — Step 3 directly clicked Send to stakeholders and immediately inspected feedback, but recorded domChanged=NO and no sent message observation.
Muted helper and no-match/result-summary text is extremely low contrast against white, reducing readability.
Instead of literal `Injected`, booked input is interpreted and renders as bold “Injected”.
Shipping Washer 11mm from 60 to 59 changed its row to Low — reorder and total units from 535 to 534, but Items low remained 2 rather than increasing to 3 as required.

Recording a shipment of 1 Washer 11mm reduces Washer from 60 to 59, decreases total units from 535 to 534, and increases the low-item count from 2 to 3. — Washer 11mm was selected, Movement was visibly set to Shipped, and Quantity was 1 (steps 7-9), but clicking Record produced domChanged=NO; the recorded observations still show Washer 60, total 535, low 2, and movements 0.

Users can select Cable 2m in the Item control to begin an adjustment. — Steps 2-11 repeatedly attempted to open or navigate the Item selector, but recorded no DOM change and observed it still displaying "BLT-04 — Hex bolt M4" rather than Cable 2m.
Outside-click dismissal is inconsistent: clicking the backdrop at (100,700) did not remove the dialog from the fresh page state; the dialog and Close button remain exposed after re-check.
All eight table steppers expose only “−” or “+”, with no item-specific accessible name, making row controls indistinguishable.

The confirmation dialog can be dismissed by Close, Escape, and clicking outside it. — Close, Escape, and outside-click dismissal were attempted in steps 14-16 with no recorded dismissal effect, and the run then attempted additional residual-dialog cleanup in steps 17-18.

Clicking Panel A3’s minus stepper changes its count from 7 to 6 and its variance from — to −1; Reset counts then restores every row to its System value with — variance. — The Panel A3 minus attempts in steps 24-26 left Panel at 7/7 with — while changing Cable 2m instead; although Reset counts was verified in step 27 to restore all four rows to System values and — variances, the required Panel A3 decrement did not occur.

Clicking Washer 11mm’s plus stepper while it is at 59/-1 restores it to 60/—. — Steps 37-38 attempt the Washer 11mm plus control from its recorded 59/-1 state, but step 39 records that the Washer-aligned plus attempt altered Hex bolt M4 instead, requiring Reset counts.
